### 2026-10-10 – # Making the schematics and PCB

**5.18h**

# Making the schematics and PCB

**Just finished making my the schematics and PCB of STARBIE!**

I used the guide on github to help me and overall it was pretty helpful!

### Schematics:
The schematics were pretty fun and easy to do (I have a Lapse of the whole process). As I was making the schematics.

As I opened the 'footprint assignment tool', and I was trying to assign each part to each other, I realised I actually forgot to download/install the footprint libraries! I was so confused, I was staring at the guide for full minutes, scratching my head figuring out why I couldn't find the controller!

 But, other than that I didn't really encounter any significant errors or issues other than silly me forgetting to connect a few wires to each part properly.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H1UNfKeiXo6fn4gM7gioqmiooX6DUU7w/7cf83641d97218c9e7f72a9ce7097576d5c007e3ebb7ca8229764a01ccb9cbf7.png)

But after that, I was done and was moving on  to the PCB!

### Making the PCB:

At first I was chugging along fine, transferring the schematics onto the PCBs. I wanted to change the layout of my Starbie, just swapping some parts' places. As I was doing this and making the physical plate, I thought this was alright, fine, chill. Until the copper wiring came... Ah hell nah. 2 different layers, blue and red, not enough space on the plate, figuring out what copper downpours are. (At one point I had 3 of the same color on there.) This tiny dreaded label called Unrouted 3,6,etc was killing me. I zoomed in and checked each and every pin for any blue line, and then it was the GND pins. I don't exactly remember what I did, but after tons of repouring and rewiring, the Unrouted label showed a big fat **0**.

But that's only part 1 brother.

The other half was facing the **Design Rules Checker**. When I finally thought it was over, I ran the test, and I was hit **10** errors and **30** warnings! I started praying that maybe I'll be able to finish this week. Google search after google search, docs and libraries, google summaries, reddit threads I finally did it. I only had the 2 errors that were acceptable, the malformed courtyard. (Whatever that means.)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H1UNfKeiXo6fn4gM7gioqmiooX6DUU7w/7cb6975a23f661b588098ac188c0ef7d6686193652ec9cef552c72652793c227.png)

I looked at mine and the guides copper connections and just wondered, how. HOW!! But  hey it's over, its behind us now (Right?!?!?)

The extra hours I put was the time required for debugging when I would pause my Lapses and debug and started on the Arduino.

## Now I have finished the hardware side, onto something I am more... confident in.
I do have some prior knowledge with Arduino Code so am excited for that! So excited I have also downloaded it and installed all the libraries, took a really long time tho.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H1UNfKeiXo6fn4gM7gioqmiooX6DUU7w/26d405118a49dff285eaf46d8a56785782760b377ae977c99573fc01defb85cf.png)

### 2026-10-11 – # Made the Arduino code, put some images on PCB and getting ready for submission

**6h**

# Made the Arduino code, put some images on PCB and getting ready for submission
**I think I have finished my project now and going to submit soon.**

## Customizing the Arduino Code.
Doing what the tutorial said, I attempted the challenges.

**Challenge 1**

 I changed the void drawSparkle function into a star itself! It is a 5-pointed star it looks like this in the green dots among the white grid. Though it looks pretty simple, I had a hard time figuring out each coordinate what dot it would fill in, but in the end after a couple of YouTube tuts I figured it out.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H1UNfKeiXo6fn4gM7gioqmiooX6DUU7w/171a9db8bb17a327a78c2ad494d8ea43634b68f6e374c6458200a2c6b007cfa5.png)

Here's the code

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H1UNfKeiXo6fn4gM7gioqmiooX6DUU7w/cd370ce35c4a30f2f213e3212e1f7cde82021d1ca92e9cac10bb84ff3c338855.png)

**Challenge 2**

For the 2nd challenge making the bitmap pet, I drew a duck as my pet. It was a 32x32 black and white duck. I hand-drew it on piskelapp.com

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H1UNfKeiXo6fn4gM7gioqmiooX6DUU7w/30393192024460c85f16dcd3fe96196973bd81970bf0e9620f18a1b96cdfe65f.png)

This challenge was much easier to do as it didn't really require any deep calculations as to where each coordinate would go. But lowkey getting the duck's bill shape to look natural took way longer than expected.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H1UNfKeiXo6fn4gM7gioqmiooX6DUU7w/645d76a46a68c03861ae18d040fe277350c8c9c8882bad339beeb2a799342c62.png)

After that I put it in this converter which would like translate the image into code i guess and pasted it into Arduino.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H1UNfKeiXo6fn4gM7gioqmiooX6DUU7w/b6a1e1a6ba73287346907fb1059daa72a200758b37861065cd9601023646e586.png)

## Putting some stickers on the PCB!

I saw everyone put like all sorts of things on their PCBs while doomscrolling, so I decided, I want to do that. To my surprise, it was easier than expected! I made a couple of images on Piskel put it on the image converter, then just pasted them in, but I did have to spend some time getting the right size though.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H1UNfKeiXo6fn4gM7gioqmiooX6DUU7w/30155ef84dc587721784269c3c538ef896ac85a97156d1705392aa7940933c4f.png)

## Finally Wrapping up this project!

All that awaited after was just exporting all the appropriate files and uploading to Github! After some YouTube tutorials and downloading the files, I was looking for the folder where I had kept my repo at. After searching for minutes, I realized *I hadn't even cloned the damn repo yet.* RAHHHHR.

Then I just cloned it and put the repo folder in some  random ahh folder so buried inside, you have to spend a full minute just dragging the file, dropping it, then repeating it until you found the repo folder.  *Never making that mistake again*

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/H1UNfKeiXo6fn4gM7gioqmiooX6DUU7w/7fea57c7e3c30814d13f513523e38397e2710f386439e13061ecac1d0a17e0c1.png)

(Oh yeah forgot to mention, I also did the README too!)

But yeah, this might be the final journal before submission for week 1!

### 2026-10-21 – # Sourcing the parts

**1.5h**

# Sourcing the parts

This entry was all about sourcing where I can find the cheapest parts to build my starbie. I looked literally everywhere, aliexpress, lscs compared them and found the cheapest possible parts. But the shipping costs, rahhhhhhhh! That's basically as much as the whole cart. I tried getting everything off the cheapest website, first i though it was going to be lcsc, but their shipping fee was TOO MUCH!! I went onto AliExpress, and guess what, NO SHIPPING FEE!! I bought almost everything from there other than the PCB itelf, i got that from JLCPCB.

Just look at the screenshots, When i was on lcsc, I saw they charge for handling fees?!?! how dare they.
Because with this, I was WAAY over the tier 1 limit. lowkey felt like i nearly got scammed.

But thanks to ALIEXPRESS, i am just under, phew!

but then i realised, that wait, im in australia, im looking at Australian dollars, the BOM is asking for it in US dollars. then i went down this absolute rabbit whole of conversion stuff, my head started hurting.

But finally it's done!
